incidents.victim: Ledger Hardware Wallet Customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely (suspected China-linked supply chain tampering)
incidents.vector: Spy chips soldered into Ledger Nano X wallets by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis intercepted seed phrases via a built-in modem and eSIM; newer implants used professional laminated flex PCBs indistinguishable from original components.
incidents.impact: Over $86 million in cryptocurrency stolen across more than a year; Ledger halted sales through CryptoBilis and advised all affected customers to replace devices and move funds to new blockchain addresses; implants also found in Ledger Flex wallets.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure VPN
incidents.vector: Three-vulnerability exploit chain in Ivanti Connect Secure: authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation chained to compromise VPN appliances without credentials; exploitation confirmed from October 1, 2026.
incidents.impact: Attackers extracted credentials, dumped Active Directory metadata, deployed custom malware, and tampered with logs; CISA added CVE-2026-104935 to KEV catalog October 13; Ivanti's own integrity checker may miss in-memory exploitation.

incidents.victim: Organizations using SonicWall SMA appliances
incidents.vector: CVSS 10.0 server-side request forgery vulnerability CVE-2026-102255 in SonicWall SMA appliances actively exploited; honeypot detections began October 9–10, 2026.
incidents.impact: Mass exploitation underway; Inc ransomware previously exploited related SonicWall SMA 1000 zero-days in July 2026; full patch availability unclear at time of reporting.

incidents.victim: Enterprise organizations globally (50,000+ exposed Citrix instances)
incidents.vector: Two chained CVSS 9.5 zero-day vulnerabilities CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway exploited for unauthenticated remote code execution; web shells deployed on compromised appliances.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation since August 21, 2026; 50,277 internet-exposed instances identified; web shells deployed enabling persistent access and lateral movement.

incidents.victim: Oracle Health (Cerner) — 20 million patients
incidents.vector: Intrusion into Oracle Health's legacy Cerner electronic health record systems; initial access vector unspecified.
incidents.impact: Personal health data of 20 million patients exposed; Oracle disclosed the breach approximately one year after it occurred, raising serious concerns about delayed breach notification.

incidents.victim: 75,000+ organizations globally (healthcare, financial services, IT in Japan, US, Australia, India)
incidents.vector: Phishing-as-a-service infrastructure (YAM Store + Iron Man System/CoGUI/Haozi) distributed over 1 billion phishing emails since January 2026 targeting Microsoft 365 and other platforms; Microsoft DCU seized infrastructure October 14.
incidents.impact: Over 1 billion phishing emails sent to 75,000+ organizations across multiple sectors; Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit disrupted the infrastructure on October 14, 2026.

incidents.victim: Windows users globally
incidents.vector: Windows Shell security feature bypass CVE-2026-96951 suppresses Mark of the Web warnings, allowing malicious downloaded files to execute without security prompts.
incidents.impact: Actively exploited before patch release; part of record October 2026 Patch Tuesday (1,413–1,417 CVEs); CISA added to KEV catalog October 13.

incidents.victim: Anywayanyday (Russian online travel agency)
incidents.vector: Unknown initial access; IT infrastructure disrupted and platform taken offline.
incidents.impact: All new ticket and hotel bookings suspended; website unavailable; coincides with widespread flight disruptions at Moscow airports from Ukrainian drone strikes.

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize Belgium)
incidents.vector: Unknown intrusion; systems taken offline as a precautionary measure, disrupting distribution centers, online ordering, and in-store pricing.
incidents.impact: Multinational grocery operations disrupted across the US, Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania; 400,000+ employees affected; delivery suspensions and outdated electronic shelf pricing reported.

incidents.victim: 70+ US companies (aerospace, energy, finance, healthcare, defense)
incidents.vector: IT workers using fabricated US identities placed at companies; US-based facilitators operated laptop farms to make overseas workers appear domestic; 85–90% of wages remitted to the DPRK regime.
incidents.impact: DOJ, FBI, and CrowdStrike announced coordinated disruption of the scheme affecting 70+ US companies; workers threatened violence when discovered; US citizens' identities stolen for vetting bypass.

incidents.victim: FBI (via Accenture-managed Oracle PeopleSoft); Boeing spin-off
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability in Accenture-managed FBI contractor systems; credential theft used to access data repositories at FBI and other targets.
incidents.impact: Personal and business data of nearly all FBI special agents stolen; Boeing spin-off extorted; Accenture dropped as FBI contractor; affiliate Edward Dubrovsky arrested on extortion charges; teen suspect 'Rey' detained in Jordan.

incidents.victim: The Foschini Group / Phase Eight, Hobbs, Whistles (UK fashion brands)
incidents.vector: Unknown initial access; IT systems taken offline at UK brands Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles under TFG London division.
incidents.impact: Multiple IT systems offline since October 12; online orders delayed; incident reported to UK authorities; no confirmed data theft at time of reporting.

incidents.victim: ccTLD registries for American Samoa (.as), Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl)
incidents.vector: Attackers modified DNS records to pass domain ownership checks and obtain valid HTTPS certificates for target domains; Google services and other organizations targeted.
incidents.impact: Three national top-level domain registries hijacked; valid certificates obtained to impersonate legitimate services; Google confirmed its services were among those targeted.

incidents.victim: French supermarkets (primarily Intermarche and other hypermarket chains)
incidents.vector: Hackers targeted internet-connected Danfoss refrigeration and freezer units running outdated firmware; devices were publicly accessible with default credentials.
incidents.impact: Temperatures raised in freezers across hundreds of French supermarkets on Sunday night; tens of millions of euros in food stock damage estimated.

incidents.victim: South Korean banks and financial companies
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese threat actor used AI tooling, including ARTEX and Claude AI agents, to automate intrusions into South Korean financial institutions.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike confirmed successful data exfiltration from multiple South Korean financial firms; South Korean authorities launched investigation; represents first publicly confirmed AI-assisted state espionage against the financial sector.

incidents.victim: Denmark — Central Population Register (8.8 million citizens)
incidents.vector: Attacker accessed Denmark's central population register via an account protected only by a '123456' password.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, and social security numbers of 8.8 million Danish citizens — both living and deceased — stolen.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Palo Alto GlobalProtect / Prisma Access VPN
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 in Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect and Prisma Access exploited to open unauthorized VPN sessions enabling ransomware deployment.
incidents.impact: Active ransomware attacks reported via unauthorized VPN access; ReliaQuest confirmed exploitation in the wild; both VPN gateways and clients require patching.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (government, manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, education) and organizations in Southeast Asia and Africa
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (Integrity Technology Group-enabled)
incidents.vector: Combined automated scanning (MicroScan tool) and hands-on intrusion techniques; LOTL methods, EBurst tool for Office 365 password spraying, SoftEther VPN for persistence; botnet infrastructure enabling covert lateral movement.
incidents.impact: Long-running campaign across US critical infrastructure and global targets; NSA, FBI, NCSC, and ACSC issued joint advisory with TTPs and IOCs on October 8, 2026.

incidents.victim: IDC Frontier Cloud (cloud infrastructure provider serving Japanese government)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack targeting cloud server infrastructure at IDC Frontier.
incidents.impact: Cloud server infrastructure disrupted; services to Japanese government customers affected; full scope of breach under investigation.

incidents.victim: SkyNet ISP (St. Petersburg, Russia)
incidents.vector: DDoS attack combined with unauthorized internal system access; BO Team claimed to have disabled 15,000+ network devices as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centers.
incidents.impact: Ongoing service disruptions since October 6 for residential and business customers; fiber outages, high latency, audio and video service failures; BO Team stated rapid recovery is not possible.

incidents.victim: Open-source developers and AI coding agent users (npm, Mastra AI, Rust arrayref)
incidents.vector: Malicious packages published to npm mimicking legitimate libraries (Axios clone + ChainDrop worm); Web3 blockchain-based C2; package documentation crafted specifically to deceive AI coding assistants; also targeting Mastra AI framework and Rust arrayref.
incidents.impact: ChainDrop worm propagated to 400+ npm packages; Mastra AI framework and Rust arrayref library also compromised; ongoing supply chain risk to AI-assisted development environments and cryptocurrency developers.

incidents.victim: Iraqi critical infrastructure (government and diplomatic sector)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing campaign using a fake Dubai Airports job recruitment lure delivered ShelbyLoader V2 malware; GitHub used as command-and-control infrastructure.
incidents.impact: ShelbyLoader V2 implants deployed against Iraqi government and critical infrastructure targets; campaign active since March 2026 and disclosed publicly in October 2026.
